newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to increase excise tax on fuels in May.
newsitem.headline: Poland to increase excise tax on fuels in May.

text.p: Poland will increase excise tax on fuels this month but not significantly and the move should not affect the price of petrol considerably, Finance Minister Marek Belka told a news conference on Wednesday.
"An increase of excise tax (on fuels) will take place soon, by the end of May. It will not be significant," Belka said.
"It will not put major upward pressure on the price of petrol" he added.
Industry sources told Reuters on Tuesday that the finance ministry was expected to raise the tax by at least three groszes per litre in the next few days.
Belka did not say by how much the tax would be increased.
The excise tax on imported fuel is now 876 zlotys per tonne of 94-octane leaded petrol, 791 zlotys per tonne of unleaded petrol and 440 zlotys per tonne of diesel.

A rise of between three and five groszes per litre, predicted by some industry sources, would entail a rise of between 30 and 50 zlotys per tonne, or three to 11 percent, depending on the kind of fuel.
The sources said that the ministry decided to raise the tax only after the country's biggest fuel refinery Petrochemia Plock agreed not to raise its prices despite the tax increase.

The head of Poland's liquid fuel chamber Andrzej Szczesniak said an excise tax rise could boost prices of imported fuel but not necessarily by the same amount as distributors could lower their margins, now at 9-15 groszes per litre.
